description: Machine-readable feature state list. Single source of truth for scope. State transitions are gated by verification: a feature only becomes 'passing' when its verification command actually passes. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: CLI accepts `npx humb <database-url>`, auto-detects the database engine from the target (Postgres today), and starts the local server.
features.evidence: commit 9c37ec2 (PR #3): pnpm --filter humb test passes (7/7, packages/cli/src/index.test.ts) on 2026-07-01. Manually re-verified end to end against a real Postgres container: `HUMB_PORT=7799 humb <url>` listened on 7799 (env var previously silently ignored, now fixed via resolvePort), and `GET /` served the built apps/web UI (previously 404'd; fixed via static serving in packages/server) with `GET /api/health` reporting `connected`.

features.behavior: Launching Humb opens the browser UI which shows the database connection status.
features.evidence: commit ec9ebf2 (PR #6): pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01 against a real Postgres container. Fixed a real infra gap along the way: Playwright's webServer only ran `vite preview` (no backend), so /api/health always failed - replaced with e2e/server.ts, which starts the real Humb server (API + built web app on one port, matching a real `npx humb <url>` launch) and connects to Postgres only when HUMB_TEST_DATABASE_URL is set.

features.behavior: Postgres adapter introspects schemas, tables, columns, indexes, and row counts.
features.evidence: commit 4ec7345 (PR #4): pnpm --filter @humbdb/db-postgres test passed (16/16) on 2026-07-01, including new integration tests (postgres-adapter.integration.test.ts) against a real Postgres container that previously did not exist for getOverview/getTable/getRows/runReadOnlyQuery. Auditing against the full spec found schemas/tables/columns were covered but indexes and row counts were entirely unimplemented (missing from @humbdb/core's TableMetadata contract and the adapter) - added IndexMetadata to @humbdb/core, index introspection via pg_index/pg_class/pg_attribute, and an approximate row count via pg_class.reltuples with a COUNT(*) fallback for never-analyzed tables (reltuples is -1 until ANALYZE runs). Manually re-verified end to end: GET /api/tables/public/humb_demo_users returned real indexes (with a genuine string[] columns array, not the raw Postgres array-literal string node-postgres returns for untyped array columns - caught and fixed via an explicit ::text cast) and rowCount 3. Package later renamed/moved packages/db-postgres -> packages/drivers/postgres (@humbdb/postgres) in commit cc3db12 (PR #5) as part of an architecture reorganization; re-verified the same 16/16 pass at the new location and updated this verification command accordingly.

features.behavior: UI shows a database navigation tree (schemas/tables) and table metadata.
features.evidence: commit ec9ebf2 (PR #6): pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01: added SchemaTree/TableDetail components (@humbdb/ui), api/hooks (apps/web), wired into App.tsx. The connect-and-inspect journey now actually clicks the fixture table in the nav tree and asserts a column name is visible (previously only asserted the table name appeared as text, which would have passed without real interaction) - strengthened per the goal-driven-execution rule rather than leaving a superficial check.

features.behavior: UI displays a paginated page of rows for a selected table.
features.evidence: commit 1f779da: pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01 against a real Postgres container: added RowsTable (@humbdb/ui), api/rows.ts + useRows hook (apps/web, using TanStack Query's keepPreviousData to avoid flicker between pages), wired into App.tsx below TableDetail with Previous/Next controls. "Can go next" uses a simple rows.length === pageSize heuristic (no exact total count from the backend) - manually verified the boundary is correct via curl with page=0/1 at pageSize=2 against the 3-row fixture. The connect-and-inspect journey now asserts real fixture row values (ada@example.com, grace@example.com) are visible, not just presence of a table.

features.behavior: Read-only SQL query runner executes SELECT-style statements and rejects mutations.
features.evidence: commit c049110: pnpm --filter @humbdb/postgres test (24/24) and pnpm --filter @humbdb/server test (8/8) pass on 2026-07-01. Auditing found a real, exploitable security bug: assertReadOnly only checked the leading keyword, so a writable CTE (`WITH deleted AS (DELETE FROM t RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM deleted`) starts with the allowed "with" keyword but actually deletes data - confirmed this executed a real DELETE through the adapter against a live table before fixing it. Fixed with two layers: assertReadOnly now scans the whole statement (literals/identifiers stripped first) for forbidden keywords anywhere, not just leading; and runReadOnlyQuery now runs inside a real Postgres READ ONLY transaction as the authoritative backstop - proved this independently with a test hiding a DELETE inside a plpgsql function call, which no string check could ever catch. Also fixed a rejected query returning HTTP 500 instead of 400 (moved ReadOnlyViolationError to @humbdb/driver-contract so packages/server can catch it without depending on a concrete engine). Built the missing UI (QueryRunner in @humbdb/ui, wired via apps/web) and manually verified success/rejection/writable-CTE cases through the real HTTP path against a live Postgres container.

features.behavior: Local server exposes health and runtime diagnostics endpoints for agent verification.
features.evidence: commit 5259102: pnpm --filter @humbdb/server test (8/8) and pnpm --filter @humbdb/postgres test (25/25) pass on 2026-07-01. Auditing /api/health (built in F001) against the full spec found a real bug, not just a coverage gap: node-postgres's Pool emits an unhandled "error" event when an idle client's connection is severed by the database (restart, network blip, admin kill) - confirmed live by starting the CLI against a real Postgres container, stopping the container mid-session, and watching the entire Node process crash instead of /api/health ever reporting "disconnected". Fixed by attaching pool.on("error", ...) in packages/drivers/postgres/src/index.ts's connect() to log instead of crash. Re-verified live: after the fix, killing the database leaves the server up and /api/health correctly returns database: "disconnected"; a subsequent SIGINT still shuts down cleanly. Added a regression test (postgres-adapter.integration.test.ts) that reproduces the exact failure via pg_terminate_backend on an idle pooled connection against a real database - confirmed it fails (uncaught exception) without the fix and passes with it.

features.behavior: CLI recognizes a SQLite file target (`npx humb ./app.db`) and the full connect-and-inspect API surface (health, overview, table metadata, paginated rows, read-only query runner) works against it with zero credentials, per docs/product-specs/connect-and-inspect-sqlite.md. Also validates the driver-plugin architecture: a second engine is what actually proves packages/drivers/<engine> is reusable, not just designed to look reusable. Playwright coverage of the SQLite journey is split out as F011 (see docs/PLANS.md's rule on splitting oversized work) - this entry covers the backend adapter + CLI wiring, verified live end to end via the real HTTP path, not just package tests.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humbdb/core test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/driver-contract test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/sqlite test && pnpm --filter humb test
features.evidence: commit 9c2162d: pnpm --filter @humbdb/core test (17/17, includes new SQLite-path parseConnectionTarget cases), pnpm --filter @humbdb/driver-contract test (21/21, includes assertReadOnly relocated here from @humbdb/postgres so both engines share one implementation instead of duplicating it), pnpm --filter @humbdb/sqlite test (12/12, including an integration test proving the read-only connection - not just assertReadOnly's string scan - is what actually refuses writes), and pnpm --filter humb test (7/7) all pass. Re-verified @humbdb/postgres (11/11) and the full connect-and-inspect Postgres journey (pnpm test:e2e:full, pnpm test:e2e) still pass unchanged after generalizing parseConnectionTarget - no regression from adding a second engine. Manually verified live end to end: built the whole monorepo, ran the real CLI (`humb ./demo.db`) against a real SQLite file, and confirmed over the real HTTP path - /api/health reports connected with the raw file path unredacted (not the Postgres-only '<unparseable connection string>' placeholder a naive reuse of redactConnectionString would have produced - caught and fixed during this verification), /api/overview returns a single 'main' schema, /api/tables/main/humb_demo_users returns correct columns/PK/rowCount, a read-only SELECT query runs successfully, and a DELETE is rejected with 400 (not 500) leaving all 3 rows intact. SIGINT still shuts down cleanly. Also verified via a direct better-sqlite3 smoke test that PRAGMA-based introspection behaves as assumed (table_info's pk field, index_list's origin='pk' only for composite/non-integer PKs, stmt.columns() works correctly on zero-row results) before relying on it in the adapter.

features.behavior: README.md accurately reflects the current product (F001-F007 passing, not a skeleton), gives a working quick-start, and includes the marketing surface needed for GitHub/npm discovery: a demo GIF or asciicast, a "why not X" comparison section, badges (CI/npm/license), and the read-only-enforced-by-the-database security story from F006/F007.
features.evidence: commit 7936c48 (PR #25, https://github.com/ensp1re/humb/pull/25): full rewrite of README.md - quick-start covers both Postgres and SQLite targets; CI/npm/license badges (shields.io, CI badge verified against the real workflow via `gh api repos/ensp1re/humb/actions/workflows`); a "Why not just use ___?" section comparing against pgAdmin/DBeaver-style GUIs, a database's own CLI, and cloud-hosted DB GUIs; the read-only-enforced-by-the-database security story (assertReadOnly's scan plus the real Postgres READ ONLY transaction / SQLite readonly:true backstop from F006/F008). Demo asset: asked the user directly whether to (a) ship static screenshots now, (b) connect the Chrome extension to record a real animated GIF, or (c) skip the visual demo entirely - chose (a), so the behavior's "demo GIF or asciicast" is satisfied with three real screenshots (not mockups) instead of an animation: new scripts/capture-readme-screenshots.mjs starts a real server against a live Postgres fixture (with an added FK-constrained table for a meaningful Schema tab screenshot) and drives a real Playwright browser through the SQL Editor/Schema/Tables tabs, saving PNGs to docs/screenshots/ (a new directory, not docs/generated/ - that's gitignored for build-time ephemera, but these need to be committed to render on GitHub/npm). An animated demo remains a legitimate follow-up. New scripts/check-readme.mjs (checks for no skeleton language, a working quick-start, >=3 shields.io badges, a screenshot section, a "why not" heading, and the read-only story) wired into a new `check:readme` script and folded into `check:state`/`pnpm check`. `node scripts/check-readme.mjs` and `pnpm check` (full monorepo) both pass.

features.behavior: `npm install -g humb` (or `npx humb@latest`) works standalone outside this monorepo: the published package serves the built apps/web UI (fixes the apps/web/dist monorepo-relative path tech debt tracked in docs/exec-plans/tech-debt-tracker.md), has npm-discoverability metadata (description, keywords, repository, homepage), and can be released via a repeatable script that bumps every publishable workspace package's version in lockstep and publishes them in dependency order.
features.evidence: commit 370c645 (PR #28, https://github.com/ensp1re/humb/pull/28): packages/cli's defaultWebRoot() located apps/web/dist via a path relative to its own file, which only resolved inside this monorepo checkout - fixed by bundling apps/web's build directly into the humb package itself via tsup.config.ts's onSuccess hook (copies apps/web/dist into packages/cli's own dist/web after a successful build, included automatically since files:["dist"] already covers the whole dist tree). defaultWebRoot(here) is now exported and takes an explicit directory instead of reading import.meta.url itself, making it a testable pure function like resolvePort/resolveFilesRoot - tries the bundled dist/web first, falls back to the old monorepo-relative path for local dev/test. turbo.json gets an explicit humb#build -> @humbdb/web#build task dependency since there's no package.json dependency edge between them for turbo to infer build order from. Added npm-discoverability metadata (keywords, homepage, repository, bugs) to packages/cli/package.json. New scripts/verify-npm-package.mjs packs the humb package exactly as pnpm publish would, extracts that tarball into a fresh temp directory with zero relationship to this repo, symlinks in the already-built workspace dependencies (real npm-registry resolution isn't possible pre-publish), and starts the real server against a real SQLite file from that standalone location - asserts GET / serves the actual UI (not a 404) and GET /api/health reports a real connection; the generated harness imports defaultWebRoot from the packed "humb" package itself via node's self-referencing package resolution, exercising the actual shipped function. Verified: rm -rf packages/cli/dist && pnpm build reproduces dist/web from scratch; node scripts/verify-npm-package.mjs passes; node scripts/publish.mjs --dry-run passes (had to temporarily relocate an unrelated pre-existing untracked CLAUDE.md out of the working tree to satisfy its clean-tree check, then restored it - confirmed via git status --porcelain unchanged after); pnpm test (all packages, including new defaultWebRoot unit tests) and pnpm test:e2e/test:e2e:full against a real postgres:16-alpine container pass; pnpm check (full monorepo) passes.

features.behavior: The Playwright connect-and-inspect journey (e2e/connect-and-inspect.spec.ts) covers SQLite, not just Postgres - parameterized by engine/fixture per docs/product-specs/connect-and-inspect-sqlite.md's "Primary end-to-end journey" section, not a duplicated spec. Split out from F008 (see that entry's evidence) because it also needs e2e/server.ts to start against either a Postgres or SQLite fixture depending on the run, which is its own real slice of work.
features.evidence: commit 126ad1b (PR #35, https://github.com/ensp1re/humb/pull/35): playwright.config.ts now runs two projects ("postgres", "sqlite") against two webServer instances (e2e/server.ts, parameterized by HUMB_TEST_SQLITE_PATH/HUMB_E2E_PORT); the @humbdb/web build step moved out of the webServer commands into the test:e2e/test:e2e:full npm scripts themselves so it runs once instead of racing two vite build processes writing dist/ concurrently. @humbdb/testing gained SQLite equivalents of the existing Postgres fixture helpers (ensureSqliteFile, setupSqliteFixture, requireTestSqlitePath) producing the same table/rows shape, so e2e/connect-and-inspect.spec.ts's assertions hold unmodified for either engine - the spec branches only its fixture setup call on testInfo.project.name, proving the UI is genuinely engine-agnostic rather than accidentally Postgres-shaped. Added the missing @humbdb/sqlite tsconfig path mapping (tsconfig.base.json) needed for tsx to resolve it from e2e/server.ts. Verified: pnpm test:e2e (both projects boot and pass @smoke); pnpm test:e2e:full against a real Postgres container (both projects pass the full journey, run twice back-to-back to confirm both fixtures are idempotent); pnpm check (full monorepo) passes.

features.behavior: The SQL Editor gains a query history drawer (icon in the toolbar, slides in from the right, one card per past query). Clicking a card prefills the editor with that query's text without auto-running it. Only successful queries are recorded, stored in localStorage (not server-side), capped at 50 entries, deduped on consecutive re-runs.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui build && pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui typecheck && pnpm --filter @humbdb/web build && pnpm test:e2e:full
features.evidence: commit 8f86d9a: new QueryHistoryDrawer (packages/ui, presentation-only) opened via a new toolbar icon button on QueryRunner (onOpenHistory callback); new useQueryHistory hook (apps/web, localStorage key humb-query-history, matches useTheme's existing localStorage pattern) capped at 50 entries, re-running a query already in history moves it to the front instead of duplicating it, only recorded on runQuery's onSuccess (never on a rejected/failed query). New e2e/query-history.spec.ts (@full) proves the run -> appears in history -> click -> prefills journey on both engine projects. Adding a second @full spec against the same live Postgres surfaced a real, pre-existing concurrency bug in @humbdb/testing's setupFixture: DROP+CREATE isn't safe under concurrent Playwright workers (two concurrent CREATE TABLEs raced pg_class's uniqueness constraint) - fixed by running the whole operation on one session under a Postgres advisory lock, benefiting every current and future @full Postgres test, not just this one. pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui build/typecheck and pnpm --filter @humbdb/web build/typecheck clean; pnpm test:e2e/test:e2e:full (both engine projects, run twice back-to-back to confirm the race fix is robust) pass; pnpm check (full monorepo) passes. Manually verified live via Preview against a real Postgres fixture: empty state before any query, a successful query appears with a correct relative timestamp, clicking a card prefills without auto-running (confirmed the stale result table stays put, proving no re-run happened), re-running the same query dedupes (still 1 entry, not 2), a rejected DELETE (blocked by read-only enforcement) is correctly never recorded, history survives a full page reload, and both light and dark mode render correctly.

features.behavior: The SQL Editor migrates from a plain <textarea> to CodeMirror 6 and gains schema-aware autocomplete: SQL keyword completion (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, etc.) and real table-name completion after FROM/JOIN, sourced from the already-fetched schema data (no new backend endpoint). Column-name completion is explicitly deferred. Existing behavior (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to run, toolbar, design tokens in both themes) is preserved exactly.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui build && pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui typecheck && pnpm --filter @humbdb/web build && pnpm test:e2e:full
features.evidence: commit d315870: QueryRunner (packages/ui) migrated from a plain <textarea> + hand-rolled gutter to CodeMirror 6 (@codemirror/lang-sql, @codemirror/autocomplete, codemirror's basicSetup for line numbers/history/bracket-matching), reskinned to docs/references/design-system.md's tokens rather than CodeMirror's default theme - verified live in both themes via Preview (keyword/table syntax highlighting in --c-purple/--c-blue/--c-green, gutter/border/selection colors all matching tokens). New packages/ui/src/sql-completion.ts (unit-tested, 8 tests): a schema-aware CompletionSource offering only the read-only-relevant SQL keywords (SELECT/FROM/WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY/GROUP BY/LIMIT/HAVING/AS/DISTINCT/AND/OR/IN/LIKE/NULL/IS - never INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, which the server rejects anyway per F006) everywhere, and real table names after FROM/JOIN, sourced from a new `tableNames` prop apps/web derives from the already-fetched schema overview (no new backend endpoint, no fetching inside packages/ui). Column-name completion is explicitly out of scope, matching the spec. Preserves the sql/onSqlChange/onRun prop contract and data-testid="query-runner" exactly, so App.tsx's usage didn't need to change shape. Found and fixed a real bug while verifying live: CodeMirror's own defaultKeymap binds Mod-Enter to insertBlankLine, which silently intercepted the Ctrl/Cmd+Enter-to-run binding before it could ever fire - confirmed via a real Playwright run (Cmd+Enter was inserting a blank line, turning a 1-line query into 2, instead of running) - fixed with Prec.highest so the run binding takes priority. Updated e2e/query-history.spec.ts's textarea-based interactions for CodeMirror's contenteditable .cm-content (page.locator(...).fill()/toHaveText, Playwright 1.49+ supports contenteditable fill); new e2e/sql-editor-autocomplete.spec.ts covers keyword completion, table-name completion, and the Ctrl/Cmd+Enter run path on both engine projects. pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui test (8/8) and build/typecheck, pnpm --filter @humbdb/web build/typecheck, pnpm test:e2e:full (both projects, run twice) and pnpm test:e2e all pass; pnpm check (full monorepo) passes.

features.behavior: MySQL as Humb's third engine (npx humb mysql://...): read-only inspection (schemas/tables/columns/indexes/row counts), paginated row browsing, and the read-only SQL query runner - reusing @humbdb/driver-contract's shared assertReadOnly heuristic plus an authoritative START TRANSACTION READ ONLY backstop (mirrors F006's Postgres precedent). Playwright coverage extends the same connect-and-inspect.spec.ts as a third project/fixture, per F011's precedent, not a duplicated spec.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humbdb/core test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/driver-contract test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/mysql test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/humb test && pnpm test:e2e:full
features.evidence: commit 9ccde55: new packages/drivers/mysql (@humbdb/mysql) implements DatabaseAdapter on mysql2/promise, mirroring @humbdb/postgres's shape - backtick identifier quoting (MySQL's own dialect, kept local to this package per ARCHITECTURE.md), information_schema introspection (explicit lowercase column aliases, since MySQL's server always returns information_schema results in UPPERCASE regardless of how the query is written - caught live via a real container), exact COUNT(*) row counts per spec, and a START TRANSACTION READ ONLY backstop in runReadOnlyQuery proven live by opening that same transaction directly (bypassing the adapter and assertReadOnly) and confirming MySQL itself still refuses a write. pool.on('error', ...) attached to the promise pool's underlying callback pool prevents a dropped idle connection from crashing the process (F007 precedent) - verified live via a real container. packages/core gained mysql:// detection; packages/cli wired mysqlAdapterFactory in. New e2e 'mysql' Playwright project/webServer; connect-and-inspect/query-history/sql-editor-autocomplete specs extended to a real 3-way branch. Found and fixed two real bugs while wiring this up: (1) every e2e webServer instance inherits every test-DB env var simultaneously, so the old 'whichever var is truthy' selection in e2e/server.ts was silently routing the new 'mysql' project to SQLite instead - fixed with an explicit HUMB_E2E_ENGINE env var per webServer entry, confirmed live via direct health-endpoint checks per port; (2) a real, reproduced concurrency bug in setupSqliteFixture (DROP+CREATE not race-safe across concurrent Playwright workers, once a third engine project pushed total parallelism higher) - fixed the same way F012 fixed the analogous Postgres bug, wrapping the whole sequence in one transaction with a busy_timeout, confirmed via 4 repeated full-parallelism runs with zero flakes afterward. Also needed a tsconfig.base.json '@humbdb/mysql' paths entry (tsx/tsc resolve every workspace package straight to source this way) and turbo.json's 'test' task env allowlist to include HUMB_TEST_MYSQL_URL. pnpm --filter @humbdb/mysql test (13/13, unit + integration against a real MySQL 8 container) and pnpm check (full monorepo) both pass; pnpm test:e2e:full (all three engine projects, run 4x) and pnpm test:e2e pass with zero flakes. Manually verified live via Preview against a real MySQL container with an FK-constrained fixture: Schema tab shows PK/FK badges correctly, Tables tab paginates rows, and the SQL Editor runs a query using a double-quoted string value (MySQL's own default dialect behavior, no adapter-side coercion needed - confirmed this is genuinely different from F018's Postgres-only fix).

features.behavior: MongoDB as a fourth engine (npx humb mongodb://...), deliberately scoped to basic read-only browsing only: databases as schemas, collections as tables, best-effort sampled field lists per collection, paginated document browsing (each page's columns are the union of fields observed on that page, not just a table-level sample). No query runner (the SQL Editor tab is not usable against a Mongo connection) and no driver-level read-only backstop - enforced instead by the adapter's code never calling any Mongo write API, explicitly weaker than every other engine's guarantee (see docs/product-specs/connect-and-inspect-mongodb.md's "Read-only enforcement" section). Depends on F016 (structured-cell viewer) shipping first - nested document fields are unusable as flat JSON text.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humbdb/core test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/driver-contract test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/mongodb test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/humb test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui build && pnpm --filter @humbdb/web build && pnpm check, plus a manual live-verification pass against a real MongoDB container (no Playwright e2e project for this engine - see evidence)
features.evidence: commit 44a4f15: pnpm --filter @humbdb/core test (22/22, incl. new mongodb://+mongodb+srv:// parsing tests), pnpm --filter @humbdb/mongodb test (14/14: factory unit tests, a source-scan test asserting the adapter calls no Mongo write API, and integration tests against a real MongoDB container covering overview/getTable/getRows/ping/version/empty-collection/BSON normalization), pnpm --filter @humbdb/humb test (13/13) all pass. pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui build/typecheck and pnpm --filter @humbdb/web build both pass (TabBar's new disabledTabs support). pnpm check (full monorepo, live Postgres+MySQL+MongoDB) passes; pnpm test:e2e:full re-run against a fresh container confirms zero regression to the other three engines' Playwright projects from e2e/server.ts's new "mongodb" HUMB_E2E_ENGINE branch (no Playwright project exercises Mongo itself - per this spec's own "decide when picked up" note, skipped for this pass: no query runner to exercise and the existing generic connect-and-inspect spec would need a Mongo-shaped fixture). Manually verified live via the Preview tool against a real MongoDB container (github pipeline mirrors this with a new mongo service in the check job): Schema tab shows the collection card with _id flagged PK and every field nullable; a nested document field renders via F016's chip and opens its inspector drawer; a Long past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER renders as an exact string and a Binary field renders as F019's binary chip with a working hex-dump-and-UTF-8-decode drawer, both reusing existing infrastructure rather than inventing new representations; the SQL Editor tab is visibly disabled (dimmed, cursor-not-allowed, unclickable) and shows an explanatory message instead of the query editor, confirmed even as the default initial tab (not just after switching away). Found and fixed BSON serialization gaps before they could surface as bugs, confirmed live against a real container first (same rigor as F019): Long/Decimal128 both serialize to useless internal shapes by default ({high,low,unsigned} and {"$numberDecimal":...}) - normalized to plain number/string/existing-binary-chip shapes; ObjectId/Date already serialize cleanly and were deliberately left untouched.

features.behavior: RowsTable and QueryRunner's result table render any object/array cell value as a compact single-line chip ({ N keys } / [ N items ]) that never grows the row; clicking it opens a right-anchored inspector drawer with an expandable tree viewer (lazy, root-expanded), replacing the old flat JSON.stringify-to-text handling in formatCell. Engine-agnostic and useful today (Postgres/MySQL json/jsonb columns already hit this path) - not Mongo-specific, though it's a hard prerequisite for F015's documents to render usably. Read-only viewing plus copy-as-JSON, no inline editing.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui build && pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui typecheck && pnpm --filter @humbdb/web build && pnpm test:e2e:full
features.evidence: commit 16dfd4b (polish on 57fd354, itself a redesign of 070f995 after user feedback that inline expansion broke the table layout): the cell is a compact chip that never grows the row (verified live: chip row 29.75px vs 27.25px plain rows) showing the count plus a dimmed truncated JSON preview for scanability; clicking opens CellValueDrawer, which closes via X/backdrop/Esc and flashes a check on copy-as-JSON. pnpm --filter @humbdb/ui test/build/typecheck and pnpm --filter @humbdb/web build all pass. pnpm test:e2e:full passes (10/12, 2 correctly skipped on sqlite/mysql) including e2e/structured-cell-values.spec.ts against a real Postgres jsonb column: chip -> drawer -> three nested levels (object -> object -> array) -> close, in both the Tables tab and a SQL Editor query result. Also manually verified live via the preview tool against a real Postgres container: drawer opens root-expanded with deeper levels lazy, syntax-colored primitives, close restores the untouched table; screenshots confirmed. Fixture: the jsonb column lives on the existing shared `humb_demo_users` table (populated for one row only) rather than a second table - a second table made the Schema tab render two table-detail cards and broke connect-and-inspect.spec.ts's singular-card assertion under concurrent @full specs (caught during 070f995's verification).

features.behavior: A single Fastify setErrorHandler normalizes every route's uncaught-error response into one consistent { error: string } shape (the real underlying message, not Fastify's generic reason phrase) - found a real bug while testing F012: POST /api/query only special-cased ReadOnlyViolationError, so any other failure (e.g. a bad table name) fell through to Fastify's default handler, and the frontend read the wrong field (body.error, literally "Internal Server Error") instead of the real Postgres message sitting in body.message. New shared ErrorState UI component (packages/ui) - occupies the same visual footprint the loaded view would, message centered, Retry action - replaces today's inconsistent inline error text across QueryRunner's result area, RowsTable, SchemaGrid, FilesBrowser, and ConsoleLog. features.behavior: The read-only query runner tolerates double-quoted string values against Postgres (e.g. `WHERE department="Support"`), which most people write out of habit even though SQL reserves "" for identifiers - Postgres alone throws `column "Support" does not exist` for it (MySQL treats "..." as a string by default; SQLite falls back to treating it as a string when it doesn't match a real identifier). Before executing against Postgres, any double-quoted token that doesn't match a real column/table name in the connected database is rewritten to an equivalent single-quoted string literal; a token that does match a real identifier (including a legitimately quoted case-sensitive column) is left untouched, so no currently-working query changes meaning. Unit tests cover doubled-quote escaping (`""` -> `"`), an embedded single quote getting escaped in the rewritten literal, a real identifier being left untouched, and a no-op when the query has no quotes. features.behavior: `redactConnectionString` (packages/core) also masks credentials passed as connection-string query parameters (e.g. `?password=...`), not just the `user:pass@host` form, so `/api/health`'s `target` field never surfaces a query-param password.
The local API server rejects requests whose `Host` header is not `127.0.0.1:<port>`/`localhost:<port>`, closing the DNS-rebinding vector against the unauthenticated localhost API.
MongoDB's `getRows` applies a deterministic sort (`_id`) so paging forward never shows a duplicate or skipped document across separate page requests.

Opening the Schema tab issues one (or a few batched) lightweight server request(s) for per-table summaries instead of fanning `useAllTables` out into one HTTP request plus several catalog queries per table, so it scales to schemas with hundreds of tables.

Postgres/MySQL connection-pool error events are routed into the server's structured `EventLog` (visible in the Console tab) instead of a bare `console.error`, so a dropped connection is visible where a user watching Console would look for it.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humbdb/postgres test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/mysql test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/server test

features.behavior: `useHealth` polls on a modest interval (matching the Console poll's cadence) instead of only fetching once on mount, so the connection indicator and the server's connection-transition log entries reflect real disconnects/reconnects without a manual Refresh.

A top-level React error boundary (plus a narrower one around the table/query result area) catches render errors and shows a recoverable fallback (reusing `ErrorState`) instead of white-screening the whole app.

Schema tree rows (`packages/ui/src/components/schema-tree.tsx`) are keyboard-focusable and operable (`Enter`/`Space` to activate, `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` to expand/collapse) with proper `role="tree"`/`role="treeitem"` and `aria-expanded`/`aria-selected` semantics.

Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB adapters set a sane default statement/query timeout (e.g. `statement_timeout`/`max_execution_time`/`maxTimeMS`, configurable) on the read-only query and row-fetch paths, so a runaway query fails fast with a clear error instead of hanging the request and holding a pool connection indefinitely.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humbdb/postgres test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/mysql test && pnpm --filter @humbdb/mongodb test

features.behavior: Overview/table/rows queries have an explicit freshness policy (a real `staleTime` and/or a light background refetch) instead of inheriting React Query's all-defaults cache, so a schema change in the connected database (table added/dropped, column changed) doesn't stay invisible until a manual Refresh.
